results.result_statement: An explicit real one-parameter family of 11-component 8-variate mixtures has fixed positive weights and distinct fixed means, covariance >= I/3, and identical moments through order four, but a varying fifth moment.

exact_retained_statements: For all d≥5 and n≥2, does V=GM_d(C^n)=closure{[exp(ℓ+q/2)]_d:ℓ∈S¹(C^n),q∈S²(C^n)} have a nondegenerate tangent map? Precisely, must T:P(V_reg)→Gr(dimV,S^d(C^n)), [v]↦T_vV, have finite fibers? The unresolved extension is beyond the proved degrees 5,…,9; [·]_d means the homogeneous degree-d part.
results.result_statement: For every d>=5,n>=2, the homogeneous Gaussian moment variety has a generically finite Gauss map; every fiber is finite within its smooth coprime finite-parameter image.
results.relation_to_original_question: All-degree generic theorem and restricted all-fiber theorem.
results.changed_assumptions: Replaces the full all-smooth-fibers assertion by generic finiteness, or by all fibers restricted to the coprime parameter image.
results.remaining_for_original_question: Treat all smooth boundary points and points lacking a coprime representation. Literal full Q741 remains partial.

exact_retained_statements: For arbitrary k, is the complexified moment map of k-component univariate Gaussian mixtures, with unknown means, variances and weights summing to 1, generically one-to-one modulo component permutation from moments m_1,…,m_{3k}? Equivalently, is the model rationally identifiable at order 3k? Algebraic finite-fiber identification at 3k−1 and rational identification at 3k+2 are established; these are not the target.

For each k≥2, are k-mixtures of gamma distributions and k-mixtures of inverse Gaussian distributions rationally identifiable from their first 3k moments, modulo component permutations? Component parameters and mixture weights are unknown. Rational identifiability refers to generic one-to-one fibers of the complexified moment parameterization; the two positive-support families are one source-conjectured target, not two counts.
results.result_statement: For each fixed k>=2 and finite moment order d, positive k-component mixture pairs in all three families satisfy parameter-mixing-measure W1=epsilon and moment difference O(epsilon^(2k-1)). No uniform inverse Holder exponent above 1/(2k-1) is possible near collisions.
results.relation_to_original_question: Residual stability obstruction; accepted exact identifiability results are unchanged.
results.changed_assumptions: Studies positive real mixing measures with deterministic moment noise and component collisions; W1 is on mean-variance parameter space.
results.remaining_for_original_question: No claim of optimal achievable exponent, separated-class stability, or sampling complexity.

results.result_statement: For an even-order real diagonal tensor with nonzero same-sign coefficients lambda_i, absence of any vanishing signed subset sum of |lambda_i|^(-2/(d-2)) implies a unique real orthogonal eigenbasis up to signs and order.
results.relation_to_original_question: Explicit sufficient criterion on a restricted tensor class.
results.changed_assumptions: Restricts to real diagonal tensors, even d>=4, all coefficients nonzero and of one sign.
results.remaining_for_original_question: Classify arbitrary PMI tensors, including necessity and other orders/sign patterns.

results.relation_to_original_question: Distribution-dependent finite determination.
results.changed_assumptions: The algebraic statement assumes all cumulants exist; its distributional interpretation assumes a CGF finite near zero.
results.remaining_for_original_question: A full distributional classification and an effective stopping certificate remain unavailable.

exact_retained_statements: For every fixed deletion probability δ∈(0,1), can a uniformly random unknown X∈{0,1}^n be reconstructed exactly from (log n)^{Oδ(1)} independent deletion traces, with success probability 1−o_n(1) over X and the channel? No polynomial-time condition is added.
results.result_statement: For a hard pair of m-bit words with t-trace TV beta, uniform n-bit reconstruction success is at most [1-2^(-m)(1-beta)]^floor(n/m). Superpolynomially small one-trace TV would rule out every polylogarithmic trace budget.

exact_retained_statements: In generalized trace reconstruction, a hidden vector p∈[0,1]^n first emits independent Bernoulli(p_i) bits, then each bit is deleted with fixed probability δ∈(0,1). If all p_i lie in {0,1/k,…,1}, what is the minimax number of traces for recovering p to ℓ∞ error below 1/(2k), with probability at least 2/3? In particular, can superpolynomial-in-n lower bounds persist for a fixed k≥2?
results.result_statement: Binary trace lower bounds transfer to every two-point Bernoulli emission alphabet; for k>=3 the fixed grid admits the interior pair {1/k,2/k}. An unconditional exponential upper bound follows from full-length traces.
results.relation_to_original_question: Model reduction and elementary finite upper bound.
results.changed_assumptions: Any binary lower-bound premise must be separately validated; the original grid itself is unchanged.
results.remaining_for_original_question: The full minimax rate and an unconditional fixed-grid superpolynomial bound remain.

exact_retained_statements: Let A receive n and one δ-deletion trace of x, and output an n-bit estimate. results.remaining_for_original_question: Fixed-deletion asymptotic constants and the deterministic worst-case frontier remain.
